message.reasoning:
I need to decide between selling a house on Illinoise Avenue or declaring bankruptcy.

Selling the house on Illinois Avenue would yield only $75. Combined with the $2 cash, that totals just $77. That is far below the $450 owed.

The mortgageable space list is empty because a house on Illinois Avenue blocks mortgaging the other red properties. I must sell that house first. Then I could mortgage Kentucky and Indiana.

The engine will apply the house sale and ask again if the debt remains unpaid. Kentucky and Indiana mortgage for $110 each, while Illinois mortgages for $120.

Even after selling the house and mortgaging all four red properties, I would only raise $417. That leaves a $33 shortfall against the $450 owed. Vermont and New York are already mortgaged, so they cannot be unmortgaged for cash.

I will declare bankruptcy. I had previously estimated maximum liquidity at $91, but that figure only included the $75 from selling the house and ignored the red properties.

I am weighing whether to declare bankruptcy now or sell assets first. If I sell the house to the bank, I receive only half its value. If I declare bankruptcy, the creditor may take the properties directly, though the exact rules vary.

I will declare bankruptcy immediately. Selling the house first would still leave a shortfall, and the cash would go to the creditor regardless.
